title.zh: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝
title.raw: 卷七 本紀第七 前廢帝 Volume 7 Annals 7: Emperor Fei I

sentences.zh: 前廢帝諱子業，小字法師，孝武帝長子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Fei I's taboo name was Ziye; his childhood name was Fashi. He was the eldest son of Emperor Xiao Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Emperor Fei, taboo name Ziye, childhood name Fashi, was Emperor Xiao Wu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年正月甲申生。

translations.literal: He was born on jia-shen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on jia-shen day in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮尋陽，子業留京邑。

translations.literal: When Shizu garrisoned Xunyang, Ziye remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu held Xunyang, Ziye stayed behind in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十年，世祖入伐元凶，被囚侍中下省，將見害者數矣，卒得無恙。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Shizu entered the capital to attack the arch-criminal, Ziye was imprisoned in the attendants' lower bureau of the Secretariat; he was nearly killed several times, but in the end came through unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when the emperor marched in against the murderer-prince, Ziye was held in the attendants' lower bureau of the Secretariat. Several times he was nearly put to death, yet in the end escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Ziye was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Ziye was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始未之東宮，中庶子、二率並入直永福省。

translations.literal: At first he did not go to the Eastern Palace; the crown prince's aides and the two commandants all entered duty at Yongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had not yet moved to the Eastern Palace; the crown prince's tutors and the two palace guard commandants were all on duty at Yongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，出居東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he took up residence in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: [1]四年，講孝經於崇正殿。

translations.literal: [1] In the fourth year, the Classic of Filial Piety was lectured on in Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: [1] In the fourth year he studied the Classic of Filial Piety in Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 七年，加元服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he received the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he underwent the capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 八年閏五月庚申，世祖崩，其日，太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year, on the day geng-shen, Shizu died; that same day the crown prince assumed the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-shen day in the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year Emperor Xiaowu died; the crown prince ascended the throne that same day.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭解尚書令，加中書監，驃騎大將軍柳元景加尚書令。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was relieved of the post of Director of the Masters of Writing and was additionally made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong stepped down as Director of the Masters of Writing and was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing instead; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 甲子，置錄尚書，太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On the day jia-zi, the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was established; Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was made Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jia-zi day the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was created, with Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong as recorder.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍柳元景加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was additionally given the rank of Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Honours Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was also granted Bearer of the Golden Halberd with honours equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Governor of Danyang Prince of Yongjia Ziren was made Inspector of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yongjia Ziren, Governor of Danyang, was appointed Inspector of Southern Yu.

translations.literal: [2] Editorial note two stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Editorial note two stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，詔曰：「朕以眇身，夙紹洪業，敬御天威，欽對靈命。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xin-wei, an edict said: "With this slight person I have long inherited the great enterprise, reverently wielding Heaven's majesty and respectfully answering the numinous mandate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xin-wei day, an edict declared: "With my slight person I have long since inherited the great enterprise, reverently wielding Heaven's majesty and answering the numinous mandate.

sentences.zh: 仰遵凝緒，日鑒前圖，實可以拱默守成，詒風長世。

translations.literal: Looking up to follow the settled tradition and daily taking the former models as my mirror, I could indeed fold my hands in silence and guard what has been achieved, passing down a lasting style.
translations.idiomatic: Upholding the settled tradition and taking former models as my daily mirror, I might indeed have folded my hands in silence, guarding what was won and passing down a lasting way.

sentences.zh: 而寶位告始，萬宇改屬，惟德弗明，昧于大道。

translations.literal: Yet as the precious throne is only now announced and the myriad realms have changed their allegiance, my virtue is not yet clear and I am obscure to the Great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as the throne is only now announced and the myriad realms have changed their allegiance, my virtue is not yet clear and I remain blind to the Great Way.

sentences.zh: 思宣睿範，引茲簡恤，可具詢執事，詳訪民隱。

translations.literal: I wish to proclaim a wise model and extend this simple compassion; let all responsible officials be consulted and the people's hardships be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to proclaim a wise model and extend this simple compassion: let every responsible office be consulted and the people's hardships be thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 凡曲令密文，繁而傷治，[3]關市僦稅，事施一時，而姦吏舞文，妄興威福，加以氣緯舛互，[4]偏頗滋甚。

translations.literal: All circuitous ordinances and secret statutes that are cumbersome and harm good governance, [3] market tolls and lease taxes imposed for a time only, yet twisted by corrupt clerks who manipulate the text and presumptuously wield authority and blessings, together with erratic cosmic signs [4] and growing partiality and excess.
translations.idiomatic: All circuitous ordinances and secret statutes that burden government, [3] market tolls and lease taxes meant as temporary measures yet abused by corrupt clerks who twist the law and presumptuously wield power, together with erratic cosmic signs [4] and ever-growing partiality.

sentences.zh: 宜其寬傜輕憲，以救民切。

translations.literal: these should be eased by lightening corvée and softening punishments, to relieve the people's urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: these call for eased corvée and lighter punishments to relieve the people's urgent distress.

sentences.zh: 御府諸署，事不須廣，雕文篆刻，無施於今。

translations.literal: The various offices of the imperial household need not be broad; carved inscriptions and seal-cut ornament have no place in the present.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices of the imperial household need not be numerous; carved inscriptions and seal-cut ornament have no place today.

sentences.zh: 悉宜并省，以酬氓願。

translations.literal: All alike should be consolidated and reduced, to answer the people's wish.
translations.idiomatic: All alike should be consolidated and reduced, to answer the people's wish.

sentences.zh: 藩王貿貨，壹皆禁斷。

translations.literal: Princely trade in goods is entirely forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Trade in goods by imperial princes is entirely forbidden.

sentences.zh: 外便具條以聞。

translations.literal: Let the outer offices draw up detailed articles and report them.
translations.idiomatic: Let the outer offices draw up detailed articles and report them.

sentences.zh: 」戊寅，以豫州之淮南郡復為南梁郡，復分宣城還置淮南郡。

translations.literal: " On the day wu-yin, Huainan Commandery in Yu Province was restored as Nanliang Commandery, and Xuancheng was again divided off to re-establish Huainan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " On wu-yin day Huainan Commandery in Yu Province was restored as Nanliang Commandery, and Xuancheng was again split off to re-establish Huainan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以南海太守袁曇遠為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day geng-chen, Administrator of Nanhai Yuan Tanyuan was made Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-chen day Yuan Tanyuan, Administrator of Nanhai, was appointed Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，鎮軍將軍、雍州刺史晉安王子勛改為江州刺史，中護軍宗慤為安西將軍、雍州刺史，鎮北將軍、徐州刺史湘東王彧為護軍將軍，中軍將軍義陽王昶為征北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day ji-hai, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Prince of Jin'an Zixun was changed to Inspector of Jiang; Central Army Guard Zong Que was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made General of the Guards; General of the Central Army Prince of Yiyang Chang was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On ji-hai day in the seventh month of autumn, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Prince of Jin'an Zixun was reassigned as Inspector of Jiang; Central Army Guard Zong Que became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Xiangdong Yu became General of the Guards; General of the Central Army Prince of Yiyang Chang became General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，婆皇國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On the day geng-xu, the state of Pohuang sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-xu day the state of Pohuang sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 崇皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The Honored Empress Dowager was styled Grand Empress Dowager; the empress was styled Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Honored Empress Dowager was elevated to Grand Empress Dowager; the empress was styled Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，罷南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On the day yi-mao, the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-mao day the northern and southern imperial speedways were abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來所改制度，還依元嘉。

translations.literal: Institutions changed since the Xiaojian era were restored to follow the Yuanjia standards.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions changed since the Xiaojian era were restored to Yuanjia standards.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，追崇獻妃為獻皇后。

translations.literal: On the day bing-chen, the late Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On bing-chen day the late Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞解領司徒。

translations.literal: On the day yi-chou, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-chou day General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan relinquished his concurrent post as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八月丁卯，領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day ding-mao, General of the Guards Wang Xuamo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on ding-mao day, General of the Guards Wang Xuamo was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: [5]己巳，以青、冀二州刺史蕭惠開為益州刺史。

translations.literal: [5] On the day ji-si, Inspector of Qing and Ji Xiao Huikai was made Inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: [5] On ji-si day Xiao Huikai, Inspector of Qing and Ji, was appointed Inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 己丑，[6]皇太后崩。

translations.literal: On the day ji-chou, [6] the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: On ji-chou day [6] the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 京師雨水。

translations.literal: Rain fell in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell in the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，[7]遣御史與官長隨宜賑卹。

translations.literal: On the day geng-yin, [7] censors were sent out with local officials to give relief as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-yin day [7] censors were dispatched with local officials to give relief as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，護軍將軍湘東王彧為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xin-chou, General Who Protects the Army Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xin-chou day, General Who Protects the Army Prince of Xiangdong Yu was appointed General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以尚書左僕射劉遵考為特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On the day gui-mao, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zunkao was made Special Grand Master and Right Honorable Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gui-mao day Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Zunkao was made Special Grand Master and Right Honorable Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，文穆皇后祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: On the day yi-mao, Empress Wenmu was enshrined beside the Jingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-mao day Empress Wenmu was enshrined at the Jingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲戌，太常建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jia-xu, Minister of Ceremonies Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jia-xu day, Minister of Ceremonies Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wu-yin, General Who Supports the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Si.
translations.idiomatic: On wu-yin day General Who Supports the State Zong Yue was appointed Inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: [8]庚辰，原除揚、南徐州大明七年逋租。

translations.literal: [8] On the day geng-chen, overdue taxes of the seventh year of Daming in Yang and Southern Xu were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: [8] On geng-chen day overdue taxes from the seventh year of Daming in Yang and Southern Xu were remitted.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙酉，以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day yi-you, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yi-you day, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was promoted to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: [9]壬辰，以王畿諸郡為揚州，以揚州為東揚州。

translations.literal: [9] On the day ren-chen, the commanderies of the capital region were made Yang Province, and Yang Province was made Eastern Yang.
translations.idiomatic: [9] On ren-chen day the commanderies of the capital region were constituted as Yang Province, and Yang Province was renamed Eastern Yang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以車騎將軍、揚州刺史豫章王子尚為司徒、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day gui-si, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang was made Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On gui-si day General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang was appointed Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang.

sentences.zh: 去歲及是歲，東諸郡大旱，甚者米一升數百，京邑亦至百餘，餓死者十有六七。

translations.literal: In the previous year and this year alike, the eastern commanderies suffered great drought; in the worst places a sheng of rice cost several hundred cash, and in the capital it also reached over a hundred; of those who starved, six or seven in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous year and this year alike the eastern commanderies suffered severe drought; in the worst places a sheng of rice cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital the price exceeded a hundred. Six or seven out of ten who starved died.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來，又立錢署鑄錢，百姓因此盜鑄，錢轉偽小，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian, mint offices had also been established to cast coin; because of this the people illicitly cast as well, so that coin grew ever more false and small and commerce would not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiaojian era mint offices had been set up to cast coin, and the people responded with illicit casting until the money grew counterfeit and debased and trade would not circulate.

sentences.zh: 永光元年春正月乙未朔，改元。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, on the day yi-wei, the first day of the month, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-wei, the first day of the first month of spring in the first year of Yongguang, the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，省諸州臺傳。

translations.literal: On the day yi-si, the provincial relay offices were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-si day the provincial relay offices were reduced.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以領軍將軍湘東王彧為衞將軍、南豫州刺史，護軍將軍建安王休仁為領軍將軍，祕書監山陽王休祐為豫州刺史，左衞將軍桂陽王休範為中護軍，南豫州刺史尋陽王子房為東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wu-wu, General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made General of the Guards and Inspector of Southern Yu; General of the Guards Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General of the Guards; Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made Inspector of Yu; General of the Left Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was made Central Army Guard; Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xunyang Zifang was made Inspector of Eastern Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On wu-wu day General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong Yu became General of the Guards and Inspector of Southern Yu; General of the Guards Prince of Jian'an Xiuren remained General of the Guards; Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was appointed Inspector of Yu; General of the Left Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan became Central Army Guard; Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xunyang Zifang was made Inspector of Eastern Yang.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，減州郡縣田祿之半。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yi-chou, the field allotments of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yi-chou day, the field allotments of provinces, commanderies, and counties were cut by half.

sentences.zh: [10]庚寅，鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: [10] On the day geng-yin, two-zhu coin was cast.
translations.idiomatic: [10] On geng-yin day two-zhu coin was cast.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰，罷臨江郡。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jia-chen, Linjiang Commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jia-chen day, Linjiang Commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，割郢州隨郡屬雍州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day ji-hai, Sui Commandery in Ying Province was detached and placed under Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on ji-hai day, Sui Commandery in Ying Province was detached and placed under Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以後軍司馬張牧為交州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bing-wu, Rear Army Major Zhang Mu was made Inspector of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: On bing-wu day Rear Army Major Zhang Mu was appointed Inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 六月己巳，左軍長史劉道隆為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day ji-si, Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Daolong was made Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on ji-si day, Left Army Chief Clerk Liu Daolong was appointed Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，安西將軍、雍州刺史宗慤卒。

translations.literal: On the day yi-hai, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Zong Que died.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-hai day General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Zong Que died.

sentences.zh: 壬午，衞將軍、南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day ren-wu, General of the Guards and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was changed to Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On ren-wu day General of the Guards and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was reassigned as Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: [11]尚書令、驃騎大將軍柳元景加南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: [11] Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was additionally made Inspector of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was also made Inspector of Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛酉，越騎校尉戴法興有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on the day xin-you, Commandant of Swift Cavalry Dai Faxing was found guilty and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on xin-you day, Commandant of Swift Cavalry Dai Faxing was found guilty and ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以尚書僕射顏師伯為尚書左僕射，[12]吏部尚書王景文為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day geng-wu, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, [12] and Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-wu day Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was promoted to Left Vice Director, [12] and Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝自率宿衞兵，誅太宰江夏王義恭、尚書令驃騎大將軍柳元景、尚書左僕射顏師伯、[13]廷尉劉德願。

translations.literal: On the day gui-you, the emperor personally led the palace guard and executed Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo, [13] and Director of Justice Liu Deyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On gui-you day the emperor personally led the palace guard and had Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Director of the Masters of Writing and General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo, [13] and Director of Justice Liu Deyuan put to death.

sentences.zh: 改元為景和元年。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to the first year of Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 文武賜位二等。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks of promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks of promotion.

sentences.zh: 以領軍將軍建安王休仁為安西將軍、雍州刺史，衞將軍湘東王彧還為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: General of the Guards Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong Yu was returned to Inspector of Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guards Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong; General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong Yu was returned to his post as Inspector of Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，司徒、揚州刺史豫章王子尚領尚書令，射聲校尉沈文秀為青州刺史，左軍司馬崔道固為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day jia-xu, Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang took charge of the Masters of Writing; Commandant of Archers Shen Wenxiu was made Inspector of Qing; Left Army Major Cui Daogu was made Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On jia-xu day Minister of Works and Inspector of Yang Prince of Yuzhang Zishang took charge of the Masters of Writing; Commandant of Archers Shen Wenxiu was appointed Inspector of Qing; Left Army Major Cui Daogu was made Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「昔凝神佇逸，磻溪讚道，湛慮思才，傅巖毗化。

translations.literal: On the day yi-hai, an edict said: "In antiquity, one concentrated his spirit and waited in retirement; at Panxi he assisted the Way. Another steeped his thought in seeking talent; at Fuyan he aided in transformation.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-hai day an edict declared: "In antiquity one concentrated his spirit and waited in retirement; at Panxi he assisted the Way. Another steeped his thought in seeking talent; at Fuyan he aided in transformation.

sentences.zh: 朕位御三極，風澄萬宇，資鈇電斷，正卯斯戮。

translations.literal: I occupy the three extremities of the throne; the winds are clear throughout the myriad realms. With axe and lightning I have cut off the guilty; at the hour mao of dawn the execution was set.
translations.idiomatic: I occupy the throne at the three extremities; order is clear throughout the realm. With axe and lightning I have struck down the guilty; at the mao hour of dawn justice was done.

sentences.zh: 思所以仰宣遺烈，俯弘景祚，每結夢庖鼎，瞻言板築，有劬日昃，無忘昧旦。

translations.literal: I think how to look up and proclaim the legacy left behind and bend down to extend the splendor of the age; night after night I dream of the ding in the kitchen, and gaze toward the builders at the ramparts—there is toil from sun to sun, and I do not forget the hour before dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I seek to look up and proclaim the legacy left behind and bend down to extend the splendor of the age; night after night I dream of the ding in the kitchen and gaze toward the builders at the ramparts—there is toil from sun to sun, and I do not forget the hour before dawn.

sentences.zh: 可甄訪郡國，招聘閭部：其有孝性忠節，幽居遯棲，信誠義行，廉正表俗，文敏博識，幹事治民，務加旌舉，隨才引擢。

translations.literal: Let commanderies and kingdoms be examined and recruits sought in the hamlets and wards: those with filial nature and loyal integrity, dwelling in seclusion and living in reclusion, with trustworthiness, sincerity, righteous conduct, integrity that sets an example for custom, literary refinement and broad knowledge, and ability to handle affairs and govern the people—let them all be especially commended and promoted according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Let commanderies and kingdoms be searched and recruits sought in hamlets and wards: those with filial nature and loyal integrity, dwelling in seclusion, with trustworthiness, sincerity, righteous conduct, integrity that sets an example for custom, literary refinement and broad knowledge, and ability to handle affairs and govern the people—let them all be especially commended and promoted according to their talents.

sentences.zh: 庶官克順，彝倫咸叙。

translations.literal: Thus officials will be able to conform and the constant relations will all be set in order.
translations.idiomatic: Thus officials will be able to conform and the constant relations will all be set in order.

sentences.zh: 主者精加詳括，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Let those in charge examine this with care and report in a manner that accords with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let those in charge examine this with care and report in a manner that accords with my intent.

sentences.zh: 」以始興公沈慶之為太尉，鎮北將軍、青冀二州刺史王玄謨為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was made Grand Commander; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji Wang Xuamo was made General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: " Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was appointed Grand Commander; General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji Wang Xuamo was made General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以石頭城為長樂宮，東府城為未央宮。

translations.literal: On the day geng-chen, Stone City was made Changle Palace and the Eastern Headquarters city was made Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-chen day Stone City was renamed Changle Palace and the Eastern Headquarters city was renamed Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 罷東揚州并揚州。

translations.literal: Eastern Yang was abolished and merged into Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yang was abolished and merged into Yang.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以北邸為建章宮，南第為長楊宮。

translations.literal: On the day jia-shen, the northern residence was made Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion was made Zhangyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jia-shen day the northern residence was made Jianzhang Palace and the southern mansion was made Zhangyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 以冠軍將軍邵陵王子元為湘州刺史。

translations.literal: General Who Champions the Army Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan was made Inspector of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Champions the Army Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan was appointed Inspector of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，原除吳、吳興、義興、晉陵、琅邪五郡大明八年以前逋租。

translations.literal: On the day bing-xu, overdue taxes before the eighth year of Daming in the five commanderies of Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langya were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On bing-xu day overdue taxes before the eighth year of Daming in Wu, Wuxing, Yixing, Jinling, and Langya were remitted.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復立南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On the day ji-chou, the northern and southern imperial speedways were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: On ji-chou day the northern and southern imperial speedways were re-established.

sentences.zh: 九月癸巳，車駕幸湖熟，奏鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day gui-si, the imperial carriage visited Hushu and music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gui-si day, the emperor visited Hushu with ceremonial music performed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On the day wu-xu, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wu-xu day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以南兗州刺史永嘉王子仁為南徐州刺史，丹陽尹始安王子真為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day geng-zi, Inspector of Southern Yan Prince of Yongjia Ziren was made Inspector of Southern Xu; Governor of Danyang Prince of Shi'an Zizhen was made Inspector of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On geng-zi day Inspector of Southern Yan Prince of Yongjia Ziren was appointed Inspector of Southern Xu; Governor of Danyang Prince of Shi'an Zizhen was made Inspector of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，撫軍將軍、南徐州刺史新安王子鸞免為庶人，賜死。

translations.literal: On the day xin-chou, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was degraded to commoner and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On xin-chou day General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was stripped of rank, reduced to commoner status, and ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以兗州刺史薛安都為平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bing-wu, Inspector of Yan Xue Andu was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On bing-wu day Inspector of Yan Xue Andu was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 丁未，衞將軍湘東王彧加開府儀同三司，特進、右光祿大夫劉遵考為安西將軍、南豫州刺史，寧朔將軍殷孝祖為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day ding-wei, General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong Yu was additionally given Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Honours Equal to the Three Dukes; Special Grand Master and Right Honorable Grand Master of the Palace Liu Zunkao was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yu; General Who Pacifies the North Yin Xiaozu was made Inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On ding-wei day General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong Yu was also granted Bearer of the Golden Halberd with honours equal to the Three Dukes; Special Grand Master and Right Honorable Grand Master of the Palace Liu Zunkao became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yu; General Who Pacifies the North Yin Xiaozu was appointed Inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以前梁、南秦二州刺史柳元怙復為梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wu-shen, former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin Liu Yuanyou was restored as Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On wu-shen day former Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin Liu Yuanyou was restored as Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 己酉，車駕討征北將軍、徐州刺史義陽王昶，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On the day ji-you, the imperial carriage campaigned against General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Yiyang Chang; within and without, the realm was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: On ji-you day the emperor marched against General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu Prince of Yiyang Chang; within and without, the realm was placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 昶奔于索虜。

translations.literal: Chang fled to the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chang fled to the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，右將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐進號鎮西大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day xin-hai, General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: On xin-hai day General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以安西長史袁顗為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day jia-yin, Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West Yuan Yi was made Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: On jia-yin day Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West Yuan Yi was appointed Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以左民尚書劉思考為益州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day wu-wu, Director of the Left Bureau of the People Liu Sikao was made Inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On wu-wu day Director of the Left Bureau of the People Liu Sikao was appointed Inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 是日解嚴，車駕幸瓜步。

translations.literal: That same day the alert was lifted; the imperial carriage visited Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the alert was lifted and the emperor visited Guabu.

sentences.zh: 開百姓鑄錢。

translations.literal: The people were permitted to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Private coinage by the people was permitted.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸亥，曲赦徐州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day gui-hai, a partial amnesty was proclaimed in Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on gui-hai day, a partial amnesty was proclaimed in Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On the day bing-yin, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bing-yin day the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 己卯，東陽太守王藻下獄死。

translations.literal: On the day ji-mao, Administrator of Dongyang Wang Zao was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On ji-mao day Administrator of Dongyang Wang Zao was thrown into prison and put to death.

sentences.zh: 以宮人謝貴嬪為夫人，加虎賁靸戟，鸞輅龍旂，出警入蹕，實新蔡公主也。

translations.literal: The palace woman Honored Consort Xie was made Lady, with tiger guards bearing halberds at the saddle, imperial carriage and dragon banners, and escort on going out and returning; in fact she was Princess Xin'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Palace woman Honored Consort Xie was made Lady, with tiger guards bearing halberds at the saddle, imperial carriage and dragon banners, and full imperial escort on going out and returning—in fact she was Princess Xin'ai.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以鎮西大將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On the day yi-you, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Honours Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On yi-you day General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army with Bearer of the Golden Halberd and honours equal to the Three Dukes.

translations.literal: [14] Editorial note fourteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.
translations.idiomatic: [14] Editorial note fourteen stands in the received text at this point in the narrative.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，寧朔將軍何邁下獄死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day ren-chen, General Who Pacifies the North He Mai was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on ren-chen day, General Who Pacifies the North He Mai was imprisoned and put to death.

sentences.zh: 新除太尉沈慶之薨。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Grand Commander Shen Qingzhi died.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed Grand Commander Shen Qingzhi died.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，立皇后路氏，四廂奏樂。

translations.literal: On the day ren-yin, Empress Lu was installed; music was performed in all four side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: On ren-yin day Empress Lu was installed, with music performed in all four side chambers of the palace.

sentences.zh: 赦揚、南徐二州。

translations.literal: Yang and Southern Xu were granted amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was proclaimed in Yang and Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍建安王休仁加特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: General Who Protects the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was additionally made Special Grand Master and Left Honorable Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Protects the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was also made Special Grand Master and Left Honorable Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 中護軍桂陽王休範遷職。

translations.literal: Central Army Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was transferred in office.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Guard Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇子生，少府劉勝之子也。

translations.literal: On the day ding-wei, a prince was born—the son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: On ding-wei day a prince was born, the son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: [15]大赦天下。

translations.literal: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: [15] A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 贓汙淫盜，悉皆原除。

translations.literal: Corruption, filth, and licentious theft were all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Crimes of corruption, debauchery, and theft were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 賜為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Those who had been made heirs for their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had been made heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以特進、左光祿大夫、護軍將軍建安王休仁為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On the day ren-zi, Special Grand Master, Left Honorable Grand Master of the Palace, and General Who Protects the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made General of Agile Cavalry and Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Honours Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On ren-zi day Special Grand Master, Left Honorable Grand Master of the Palace, and General Who Protects the Army Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was appointed General of Agile Cavalry with Bearer of the Golden Halberd and honours equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先、安南侯敬淵並賜死。

translations.literal: On the day wu-wu, Prince of Nanping Jingyou, Prince of Luling Jingxian, and Marquis of Annan Jingyuan were all ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: On wu-wu day Prince of Nanping Jingyou, Prince of Luling Jingxian, and Marquis of Annan Jingyuan were all ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 時帝凶悖日甚，誅殺相繼，內外百司，不保首領。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's ferocity and perversity grew daily worse; executions followed one after another, and within and without the hundred offices no one could keep his head.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor's ferocity and perversity grew worse by the day. Executions followed one after another, and throughout the bureaucracy no one could be sure of keeping his life.

sentences.zh: 先是訛言云：「湘中出天子。

translations.literal: Earlier a rumor had said: "A Son of Heaven will arise in Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rumor had spread: "A Son of Heaven will arise in Xiang.

sentences.zh: 」帝將南巡荊、湘二州以厭之。

translations.literal: " The emperor intended to tour Jing and Xiang to suppress it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang to counter the omen.

sentences.zh: 先欲誅諸叔，然後發引。

translations.literal: He first wished to execute his uncles and only then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He intended first to execute his uncles and only then depart.

sentences.zh: 太宗與左右阮佃夫、王道隆、李道兒密結帝左右壽寂之、姜產之等十一人，謀共廢帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming secretly joined with his attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er to ally with the emperor's own attendants Shou Jizhi, Jiang Chanzhi, and eleven others in all, plotting together to depose the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming secretly allied with his attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er, and with eleven of the emperor's own attendants including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chanzhi, to plot the emperor's deposition.

sentences.zh: 戊午夜，帝於華林園竹林堂射鬼。

translations.literal: At midnight on the day wu-wu, the emperor was at the Bamboo Grove Hall of Hualin Park shooting at ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on wu-wu day the emperor was in the Bamboo Grove Hall of Hualin Park shooting at ghosts.

sentences.zh: 時巫覡云：「此堂有鬼。

translations.literal: At the time the shamans had said: "This hall has ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: The shamans had said that ghosts haunted the hall.

sentences.zh: 」故帝自射之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the emperor shot at them himself.
translations.idiomatic: That was why the emperor went to shoot at them himself.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之懷刀直入，姜產之為副。

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi, carrying a blade, went straight in; Jiang Chanzhi was his assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi, blade in hand, went straight in; Jiang Chanzhi followed as his assistant.

sentences.zh: 帝欲走，寂之追而殞之。

translations.literal: The emperor tried to flee; Jizhi pursued him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried to flee, but Jizhi pursued him and struck him down.

sentences.zh: 時年十七。

translations.literal: He was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventeen years old.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令曰：

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order:
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order:

sentences.zh: 司徒領護軍八座：子業雖曰嫡長，少稟凶毒，不仁不孝，著自髫齔。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, Director of the Guards, and the Eight Dignitaries: Although Ziye was called the eldest son of the proper wife, from youth he bore a fierce and poisonous nature; lack of benevolence and lack of filial piety were evident from his childhood locks.
translations.idiomatic: To the Minister of Works, Director of the Guards, and the Eight Dignitaries: Although Ziye was the eldest son of the proper wife, from childhood he showed a fierce and poisonous nature; his want of benevolence and filial piety was evident even in his boyhood.

sentences.zh: 孝武棄世，屬當辰曆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiao Wu passed from the world, the turn of the celestial sequence fell to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiao Wu died, the turn of the celestial sequence fell to him.

sentences.zh: 自梓宮在殯，喜容靦然，天罰重離，歡恣滋甚。

translations.literal: From the time the imperial coffin was still in mourning, his face was bright with joy; Heaven's punishment struck the two Li trigrams, yet his wanton delight only grew.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the imperial coffin lay in mourning his face was bright with joy; though Heaven's punishment had struck the two Li trigrams, his wanton delight only grew.

sentences.zh: 逼以內外維持，忍虐未露，而凶慘難抑，一旦肆禍，遂縱戮上宰，殄害輔臣。

translations.literal: Pressed by the need to maintain appearances within and without, he restrained his cruelty and it had not yet shown; but his savage depravity could not be checked, and in a single day he unleashed disaster, then wantonly slaughtered the chief minister and annihilated his assisting ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the need to keep up appearances at court and abroad, he held his cruelty in check until it had not yet fully shown; but his savage depravity could not be restrained, and in a single day he unleashed catastrophe, wantonly slaughtering the chief minister and destroying his chief counselors.

sentences.zh: 子鸞兄弟，先帝鍾愛，含怨既往，枉加屠酷。

translations.literal: The brothers Ziluan and the rest had been dearly loved by the late emperor; nursing old grievances, he wrongly subjected them to cruel slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Ziluan and his brothers had been dearly loved by the late emperor; nursing old grievances, the emperor wrongly subjected them to cruel slaughter.

sentences.zh: 昶茂親作扞，橫相徵討。

translations.literal: Chang, a close kinsman on the maternal side, had served as a shield, yet was attacked and sent on punitive expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, a close maternal kinsman who had served as a bulwark, was nonetheless attacked and driven out on punitive expeditions.

sentences.zh: 新蔡公主逼離夫族，幽置深宮，詭云薨殞。

translations.literal: Princess Xin'ai was forced away from her husband's clan and secretly placed deep in the palace; it was falsely announced that she had died.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xin'ai was torn from her husband's clan and hidden deep in the palace, while a false report announced her death.

sentences.zh: 襄事甫爾，喪禮頓釋，昏酣長夜，庶事傾遺。

translations.literal: The mourning rites had barely ended when he abruptly cast off funeral observance; drunk and dazed through long nights, he neglected every affair.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning rites had barely ended when he cast off funeral observance; drunk and dazed through long nights, he neglected every duty of state.

sentences.zh: 朝賢舊勳，棄若遺土。

translations.literal: Worthy ministers of long service he cast aside as if they were waste soil.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy ministers of long service he cast aside like waste soil.

sentences.zh: 管絃不輟，珍羞備膳。

translations.literal: Pipes and strings never ceased; rare delicacies filled the tables.
translations.idiomatic: Music never ceased; rare delicacies filled the tables.

sentences.zh: 詈辱祖考，以為戲謔。

translations.literal: He reviled and insulted his ancestors and forebears, making them the stuff of jest.
translations.idiomatic: He reviled his ancestors and forebears, making them the stuff of jest.

sentences.zh: 行游莫止，淫縱無度。

translations.literal: His comings and goings had no restraint; his lewdness and excess knew no bounds.
translations.idiomatic: His comings and goings knew no restraint; his lewdness and excess knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 肆宴園陵，規圖發掘。

translations.literal: He held feasts in the imperial tombs and parks and plotted to excavate them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted in the imperial tombs and parks and plotted their excavation.

sentences.zh: 誅剪無辜，籍略婦女。

translations.literal: He executed the innocent without cause and seized women by force.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the innocent without cause and seized women by force.

sentences.zh: 建樹偽豎，莫知誰息。

translations.literal: He raised false attendants, and no one knew who might be spared.
translations.idiomatic: He raised false favorites, and no one knew who might be spared.

sentences.zh: 拜嬪立后，慶過恒典。

translations.literal: In appointing consorts and establishing an empress, the celebrations exceeded the constant precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing consorts and establishing an empress, the celebrations exceeded all precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗室密戚，遇若婢僕，鞭捶陵曳，無復尊卑。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and close kin he treated like maidservants and slaves, beating and dragging them with no regard for rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and close kin he treated like maidservants and slaves, beating and dragging them without regard for rank.

sentences.zh: 南平一門，特鍾其酷。

translations.literal: The house of Nanping in particular received his special cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Nanping in particular bore the brunt of his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 反天滅理，顯暴萬端。

translations.literal: He reversed Heaven and extinguished principle; his open violence had ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: He reversed Heaven and extinguished moral principle; his open violence took ten thousand forms.

sentences.zh: 苛罰酷令，終無紀極，夏桀、殷辛，未足以譬。

translations.literal: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no limit; Xia Jie and Yin Xin would not suffice for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh punishments and cruel ordinances knew no limit; even Xia Jie and King Zhou of Shang would not suffice for comparison.

sentences.zh: 闔朝業業，人不自保，百姓遑遑，手足靡厝。

translations.literal: Throughout the court, each man in his place, no one could keep himself safe; the common people in alarm could not find a place for hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the court no one in his place could keep himself safe; the common people, in alarm, could not find a place to set hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 行穢禽獸，罪盈三千。

translations.literal: His conduct was the filth of birds and beasts; his crimes filled the three thousand categories.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was filthier than birds and beasts; his crimes filled the three thousand categories of the law.

sentences.zh: 高祖之業將泯，七廟之享幾絕。

translations.literal: The enterprise of High Founder was about to perish; the sacrifices of the seven temples were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The enterprise of the dynastic founder was about to perish; the sacrifices of the seven temples were nearly extinguished.

sentences.zh: 吾老疾沈篤，每規禍鴆，憂煎漏刻，氣命無幾。

translations.literal: I am old and my illness is deep and grave; every day I foresee this calamitous poison; worry burns through each quarter of the day, and my breath and life will not last long.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and my illness is deep and grave; every day I foresee this calamitous poison. Worry burns through each quarter of the day, and my life will not last long.

sentences.zh: 開闢以降，所未嘗聞。

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age, such a thing has never been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Since the opening of the age, such a thing has never been heard of.

sentences.zh: 遠近思奮，十室而九。

translations.literal: Near and far alike yearn to rise up; nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far alike yearn to rise up—nine houses in ten.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍湘東王體自太祖，天縱英聖，文皇鍾愛，寵冠列藩。

translations.literal: General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong, by descent from Taizu, was by Heaven endowed with heroic sagacity; Emperor Wen cherished him, and his favor surpassed the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guards Prince of Xiangdong, a descendant of Taizu, was by Heaven endowed with heroic sagacity. Emperor Wen cherished him, and his favor surpassed all other princes.

sentences.zh: 吾早識神睿，特兼常禮。

translations.literal: I early recognized his divine perspicacity and treated him with special courtesy beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: I early recognized his divine perspicacity and treated him with courtesy beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 潛運宏規，義士投袂，獨夫既殞，懸首白旗，社稷再興，宗祏永固，人鬼屬心，大命允集。

translations.literal: He secretly carried out a great design; men of righteousness rallied to him. Once the tyrant had fallen, his severed head hung from the white banner; the altars of state were renewed, the ancestral temple secured forever; the hearts of men and ghosts turned to him, and the great mandate was duly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly carried out a great design, and men of righteousness rallied to him. Once the tyrant had fallen, his severed head hung from the white banner; the altars of state were renewed and the ancestral temple secured; the hearts of men and ghosts turned to him, and the great mandate was duly gathered.

sentences.zh: 且勳德高邈，大業攸歸，宜遵漢、晉，纂承皇極。

translations.literal: Moreover, his merit and virtue are lofty and far-reaching; the great enterprise is properly his. He should follow Han and Jin and succeed to the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his merit and virtue are lofty and far-reaching, and the great enterprise is properly his. He should follow Han and Jin in succeeding to the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 主者詳舊典以時奉行。

translations.literal: Let those in charge examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Let those in charge examine the old statutes and carry them out in timely fashion.

sentences.zh: 未亡人餘年不幸嬰此百艱，永尋情事，雖存若殞。

translations.literal: The one who has not yet perished, in the remaining years of her misfortune, has met this hundredfold hardship; forever recalling the circumstances, though she lives she is as if dead.
translations.idiomatic: I, who have not yet perished, in the remaining years of my misfortune have met this hundredfold hardship; forever recalling the circumstances, though I live I am as if dead.

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 當復奈何！

translations.literal: What is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done!

sentences.zh: 葬廢帝丹陽秣陵縣南郊壇西。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling County, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling County, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而狷急，在東宮每為世祖所責。

translations.literal: The emperor from youth was impatient and narrow; in the Eastern Palace he was often rebuked by Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor was impatient and narrow-tempered; in the Eastern Palace he was often rebuked by Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 世祖西巡，子業啟參承起居，書迹不謹，上詰讓之。

translations.literal: When Shizu toured the west, Ziye presented memorials on daily affairs and conduct; his handwriting was not careful, and the emperor interrogated and reproved him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu toured the west, Ziye sent memorials reporting on daily affairs and conduct. His handwriting was careless, and the emperor interrogated and reproved him.

sentences.zh: 子業啟事陳謝，上又答曰：「書不長進，此是一條耳。

translations.literal: Ziye submitted a memorial apologizing; the emperor again replied: "Your writing does not improve—this is one matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye submitted a memorial of apology; the emperor replied again: "Your writing does not improve—this is one matter.

sentences.zh: 聞汝素都懈怠，狷戾日甚，何以頑固乃爾邪！

translations.literal: I hear that you have always been negligent and indolent, and that your perversity grows worse by the day—why are you so obstinately wicked!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear that you have always been negligent and indolent, and that your perversity grows worse by the day—why are you so obstinately wicked!"

sentences.zh: 」初踐阼，受璽紱，悖然無哀容。

translations.literal: When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and cord, his face was perverse and without a look of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and cord, his face showed perversity and not a trace of mourning.

sentences.zh: 始猶難諸大臣及戴法興等，既殺法興，諸大臣莫不震懾。

translations.literal: At first he still feared the great ministers and Dai Faxing and the rest; after he killed Faxing, the great ministers were all struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: At first he still feared the great ministers and Dai Faxing and the rest; after he killed Faxing, none of the great ministers were free from terror.

sentences.zh: 於是又誅羣公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again executed the host of nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he executed the host of nobles.

sentences.zh: 元凱以下，皆被毆捶牽曳。

translations.literal: From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten, dragged, and pulled about.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten, dragged, and hauled about.

sentences.zh: 內外危懼，殿省騷然。

translations.literal: Within and without there was peril; the halls and offices were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without there was peril; the halls and offices were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 初太后疾篤，遣呼帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Empress Dowager's illness was grave, she sent to summon the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Empress Dowager's illness was grave, she sent to summon the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「病人間多鬼，可畏，那可往。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sickrooms are full of ghosts—how frightening! How could I go there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Sickrooms are full of ghosts—how frightening! How could I go there?"

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，語侍者：「將刀來，破我腹，那得生如此寧馨兒！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager in anger said to her attendants: "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a fine fragrant son!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said in anger to her attendants: "Bring a knife and cut open my belly—how could I have borne such a precious darling of a son!"

sentences.zh: 」及太后崩後數日，帝夢太后謂之曰：「汝不孝不仁，本無人君之相。

translations.literal: Several days after the Empress Dowager died, the emperor dreamed that the Empress Dowager said to him: "You are unfilial and unkind; by nature you lack the aspect of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Several days after the Empress Dowager died, the emperor dreamed that she said to him: "You are unfilial and unkind; by nature you lack the bearing of a ruler.

sentences.zh: 子尚愚悖如此，亦非運祚所及。

translations.literal: Zishang is foolish and perverse like this; he too is not what the mandate of fortune would reach.
translations.idiomatic: Zishang is as foolish and perverse as this; he too is not one whom the mandate of fortune would reach.

sentences.zh: 孝武險虐滅道，怨結人神，兒子雖多，並無天命。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao Wu was dangerous and cruel, extinguishing the Way; resentment joined men and spirits. Though he had many sons, none had Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiao Wu was dangerous and cruel, extinguishing the Way, and resentment joined men and spirits. Though he had many sons, none had Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 大運所歸，應還文帝之子。

translations.literal: To whom the great fortune belongs, it should return to a son of Emperor Wen."
translations.idiomatic: To whom the great fortune belongs, it should return to a son of Emperor Wen."

sentences.zh: 」其後湘東王紹位，果文帝子也。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince of Xiangdong Yu took the throne, and indeed he was a son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Prince of Xiangdong Yu took the throne, and indeed he was a son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 故帝聚諸叔京邑，慮在外為患。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing they would become a threat if left abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing they would become a threat if left in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 山陰公主淫恣過度，謂帝曰：「妾與陛下，雖男女有殊，俱託體先帝。

translations.literal: Princess Shanyin was licentious beyond measure and said to the emperor: "Your servant and Your Majesty, though male and female differ, alike owe our bodies to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Shanyin was licentious beyond measure and said to the emperor: "Your servant and Your Majesty, though we differ as man and woman, alike owe our bodies to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下六宮萬數，而妾唯駙馬一人。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ten thousand women in the six palaces, while your servant has only one husband.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ten thousand women in the six palaces, while I have only one husband.

sentences.zh: 事不均平，一何至此！

translations.literal: Matters are so unequal—how could it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The inequality is outrageous—how could it come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃為主置面首左右三十人；

translations.literal: The emperor then set up thirty male favorites for the princess as her attendants;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then set up thirty male favorites for the princess as her personal attendants;

sentences.zh: 進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王，食湯沐邑二千戶，[16]給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: she was advanced in rank to Princess of Kuaiji, with precedence equal to a prince of a commandery, a fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance, [16] with one set of ceremonial music, and twenty guards with ceremonial swords added.
translations.idiomatic: she was advanced in rank to Princess of Kuaiji with precedence equal to a commandery prince, a fief of two thousand households for maintenance, [16] one set of ceremonial music, and twenty guards with ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，與朝臣常共陪輦。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, he and the court ministers commonly accompanied the carriage together.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out, he commonly had court ministers accompany his carriage together.

sentences.zh: 主以吏部郎褚淵貌美，就帝請以自侍，帝許之。

translations.literal: The princess, because Director of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan was handsome in appearance, asked the emperor to have him serve her; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Because Director of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan was handsome, the princess asked the emperor to have him serve her, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 淵侍主十日，備見逼迫，誓死不回，遂得免。

translations.literal: Yuan attended the princess for ten days, was fully subjected to coercion, vowed he would rather die and would not yield, and thus was released.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan attended the princess for ten days, was relentlessly coerced, vowed he would rather die than yield, and thus was released.

sentences.zh: 帝所幸閹人華願兒，官至散騎常侍，加將軍帶郡。

translations.literal: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the emperor favored, reached the post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and was made a general with a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Hua Yuan'er, whom the emperor favored, rose to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and was made a general with a commandery attached.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書，[17]頗識古事，自造世祖誄及雜篇章，往往有辭采。

translations.literal: The emperor from youth loved reading [17] and knew the ancient affairs quite well; he himself composed the eulogy for Shizu and miscellaneous pieces, which often had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor loved reading [17] and knew ancient affairs quite well; he himself composed the eulogy for Emperor Xiaowu and miscellaneous pieces that often showed literary polish.

sentences.zh: 以魏武帝有發丘中郎將、摸金校尉，乃置此二官。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had the offices of Director of the Middle in the Mound and Colonel Who Gropes for Gold, he established these two offices.
translations.idiomatic: Because Emperor Wu of Wei had established the offices of Director of the Middle in the Mound and Colonel Who Gropes for Gold, he set up these two offices as well.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were placed in charge of them.

sentences.zh: [18]其餘事迹，分見諸列傳。

translations.literal: [18] His remaining deeds are treated separately in the various biographies.
translations.idiomatic: [18] His remaining deeds are treated separately in the various biographies.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：廢帝之事行著于篇。

translations.literal: The historian says: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: The deeds of the deposed emperor are set forth in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 若夫武王數殷紂之釁，不能絓其萬一；

translations.literal: When King Wu of Zhou counted the crimes of King Zhou of Shang, he could not bind up one ten-thousandth of them;
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Zhou counted the crimes of King Zhou of Shang, he could not bind up one ten-thousandth of them;

sentences.zh: 霍光書昌邑之過，未足舉其毫釐。

translations.literal: when Huo Guang wrote out the faults of Marquis of Haiyang, he could not raise one hair's breadth of them.
translations.idiomatic: when Huo Guang set down the faults of Marquis of Haiyang, he could not raise one hair's breadth of them.

sentences.zh: 假以中才之君，有一于此，足以霣社殘宗，汚宮瀦廟，況總斯惡以萃一人之體乎！

translations.literal: Suppose a ruler of middling talent had one of these— it would suffice to destroy the altars and ruin the clan, defile the palace and foul the temple ponds; how much more when all these evils were gathered in the body of a single man!
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a ruler of middling talent had even one of these—it would suffice to destroy the altars and ruin the clan, defile the palace and foul the temple ponds; how much more when all these evils were gathered in the body of a single man!

sentences.zh: 其得亡亦為幸矣。

translations.literal: That he escaped destruction was also a piece of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That he escaped destruction was itself a kind of fortune.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Editorial section: textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 出居東宮 各本並脫「居」字，據元龜二五六補。

translations.literal: "Moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace": all editions alike omit the character ju; supplied on the authority of Yuan Gui 256.
translations.idiomatic: On "moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace": all editions omit ju; the character is restored from Yuan Gui 256.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹永嘉王子仁為南豫州刺史 「南豫」子仁傳作「南兗」。

translations.literal: "Governor of Danyang Prince of Yongjia Ziren was made Inspector of Southern Yu": in Ziren's biography "Southern Yu" appears as "Southern Yan."
translations.idiomatic: On "Governor of Danyang Prince of Yongjia Ziren was made Inspector of Southern Yu": Ziren's biography reads "Southern Yan" instead.

sentences.zh: 繁而傷治 「傷」各本並作「作」，據元龜一九一改。

translations.literal: "Cumbersome and harm governance": for shang all editions alike read zuo; changed on the authority of Yuan Gui 191.
translations.idiomatic: On "cumbersome and harm governance": all editions read zuo for shang; emended per Yuan Gui 191.

sentences.zh: 氣緯舛互 「互」各本並作「玄」，蓋形近而譌，今改正。

translations.literal: "Erratic cosmic signs": for hu all editions alike read xuan; probably a graphic confusion of similar forms—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "erratic cosmic signs": all editions read xuan for hu, likely a graphic confusion; now corrected.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍王玄謨為鎮北將軍青冀二州刺史 各本「鎮北將軍」下並衍「南徐州刺史新安王子鸞為」十一字。

translations.literal: "General of the Guards Wang Xuamo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji": below "General Who Pacifies the North" all editions alike have an interpolation of eleven characters, "Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was."
translations.idiomatic: On "General of the Guards Wang Xuamo was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji": all editions interpolate eleven spurious characters after "General Who Pacifies the North"—"Inspector of Southern Xu Prince of Xin'an Ziluan was."

sentences.zh: 按新安王子鸞傳，不言曾為青、冀二州刺史，而王玄謨傳，言玄謨時徙為青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Prince of Xin'an Ziluan, it does not say that he ever was Inspector of Qing and Ji, whereas in the biography of Wang Xuamo it says that at this time Xuamo was transferred to Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xin'an Ziluan's biography does not record him as Inspector of Qing and Ji, whereas Wang Xuamo's biography states that Xuamo was then transferred to Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 今訂正。

translations.literal: Now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The text is now emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 己丑 各本並作「己未」。

translations.literal: "Ji-chou": all editions alike read "ji-wei."
translations.idiomatic: On ji-chou: all editions read ji-wei.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，二十三日己丑，無己未、乙丑。

translations.literal: For this month ding-mao is the first day of the month; the twenty-third day is ji-chou—there is no ji-wei or yi-chou.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on ding-mao; the twenty-third day was ji-chou—neither ji-wei nor yi-chou occurs.

sentences.zh: 今據建康實錄及通鑑改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected on the authority of the Veritable Records of Jiankang and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Now corrected per the Veritable Records of Jiankang and Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 庚寅 各本並作「庚子」。

translations.literal: "Geng-yin": all editions alike read "geng-zi."
translations.idiomatic: On geng-yin: all editions read geng-zi.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁卯朔，無庚子，二十三日己丑後，二十四日有庚寅。

translations.literal: For this month ding-mao is the first day of the month; there is no geng-zi; after the twenty-third day ji-chou, the twenty-fourth day is geng-yin.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on ding-mao, so geng-zi is impossible; after ji-chou on the twenty-third, the twenty-fourth is geng-yin.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Now corrected.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍宗越為司州刺史 「宗越」書中多誤作「宋越」，今據宗越傳改正。

translations.literal: "General Who Supports the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Si": in the book "Zong Yue" is often wrongly written as "Song Yue"; now corrected on the authority of the biography of Zong Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On "General Who Supports the State Zong Yue was made Inspector of Si": the text often miswrites Zong Yue as Song Yue; corrected per his biography.

sentences.zh: 以下類此者皆逕改，不具校。

translations.literal: Similar cases below are all directly emended without full collation being given.
translations.idiomatic: Similar cases below are emended directly without full collation.

sentences.zh: 以尚書右僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射 「尚書僕射」各本作「尚書左僕射」，南史無「左」字。

translations.literal: "Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing": in all editions "Vice Director of the Masters of Writing" reads "Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing"; the History of the Southern Dynasties has no character zuo.
translations.idiomatic: On "Right Vice Director Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing": all editions read Left Vice Director; the History of the Southern Dynasties lacks zuo.

sentences.zh: 李慈銘宋書札記云：「左字衍，當據南史刪。

translations.literal: Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Song says: "The character zuo is superfluous and should be deleted on the authority of the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Song states: "The character zuo is superfluous and should be deleted per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 」按是時但置尚書僕射，不分立左右。

translations.literal: " According to this period, only Vice Directors of the Masters of Writing were established, without separate left and right.
translations.idiomatic: " At this time only Vice Directors of the Masters of Writing were established, without separate left and right posts.

sentences.zh: 今據南史刪「左」字。

translations.literal: Now the character zuo is deleted on the authority of the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo is now deleted per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 減州郡縣田祿之半 宋本、三朝本、北監本、毛本及南史作「田祿」。

translations.literal: "The field allotments of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half": the Song edition, Three-Reigns edition, Beijian edition, Mao edition, and History of the Southern Dynasties read tian lu.
translations.idiomatic: On "field allotments of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half": the Song, Three-Reigns, Beijian, and Mao editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties read tian lu.

sentences.zh: 殿本、局本作「田租」。

translations.literal: The Palace edition and Bureau edition read tian zu.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace and Bureau editions read tian zu.

sentences.zh: 建康實錄作「祿秩」。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of Jiankang read lu zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of Jiankang read lu zhi.

sentences.zh: 按普減國內田租之半，非封建統治者所肯為，此必減州郡縣官吏田祿之半。

translations.literal: According to this, a general reduction of land tax throughout the realm by half is not something a feudal ruler would consent to; this must mean reducing the field allotments of provincial, commandery, and county officials by half.
translations.idiomatic: A general halving of land tax empire-wide is not something a feudal ruler would accept; the passage must mean halving the field allotments of provincial, commandery, and county officials.

sentences.zh: 故建康實錄改稱為「祿秩」。

translations.literal: Therefore the Veritable Records of Jiankang changed the wording to "salary ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Veritable Records of Jiankang uses "salary ranks" instead.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍南豫州刺史湘東王彧改為雍州刺史 各本並脫「南」字。

translations.literal: "General of the Guards and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was changed to Inspector of Yong": all editions alike omit the character nan.
translations.idiomatic: On "General of the Guards and Inspector of Southern Yu Prince of Xiangdong Yu was changed to Inspector of Yong": all editions omit nan.

sentences.zh: 按明帝紀，永光元年為南豫州刺史，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: According to the annals of Emperor Ming, in the first year of Yongguang he was Inspector of Southern Yu, garrisoning Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's annals record that in the first year of Yongguang he was Inspector of Southern Yu, garrisoning Gushu.

sentences.zh: 又按州郡志，此時南豫州鎮姑孰，而豫州則未嘗以姑孰為州治。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies, at this time Southern Yu garrisoned Gushu, whereas Yu had never taken Gushu as its seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies shows Southern Yu at Gushu at this time, while Yu had never had Gushu as its seat.

sentences.zh: 今據明帝紀補。

translations.literal: Now supplied on the authority of the annals of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Nan is now restored per Emperor Ming's annals.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射顏師伯 「尚書左僕射」各本並作「尚書僕射」，據南史改，說見前。

translations.literal: "Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo": in all editions "Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing" reads "Vice Director of the Masters of Writing"; changed on the authority of the History of the Southern Dynasties, as explained above.
translations.idiomatic: On "Left Vice Director Yan Shibo": all editions read Vice Director without zuo; emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties, as explained above.

sentences.zh: 以鎮西大將軍豫州刺史山陽王休祐為鎮軍大將軍開府儀同三司 鎮西大將軍各本並作「鎮北大將軍」。

translations.literal: "General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Honours Equal to the Three Dukes": in all editions "General Who Pacifies the West" reads "General Who Pacifies the North."
translations.idiomatic: On "General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yu Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Bearer of the Golden Halberd with Honours Equal to the Three Dukes": all editions read General Who Pacifies the North for General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 上九月辛亥下作鎮西大將軍，休祐傳亦作鎮西，今改正。

translations.literal: Below, under the ninth month xin-hai, it reads General Who Pacifies the West, and Xiuyou's biography also reads Pacifies the West; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The entry under ninth-month xin-hai reads General Who Pacifies the West, and Xiuyou's biography agrees; now corrected.

sentences.zh: 少府劉勝之子也 「劉勝」元龜一九七及二０七同本紀。

translations.literal: "The son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng": for "Liu Sheng," Yuan Gui 197 and 207 agree with this annal.
translations.idiomatic: On "the son of Director of the Palace Treasury Liu Sheng": Yuan Gui 197 and 207 agree with this annal for Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 符瑞志及始安王休仁傳、宋略、南史帝紀作劉矇，南史休仁傳作劉蒙。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Omens, the biography of Prince of Shi'an Xiuren, the Song Summary, and the imperial annals in the History of the Southern Dynasties read Liu Meng; the biography of Xiuren in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Liu Meng with a different homophonous graph.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Omens, Prince of Shi'an Xiuren's biography, the Song Summary, and the Southern Dynasties annals read Liu Meng; Xiuren's biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties gives the name with a different homophonous graph.

sentences.zh: 食湯沐邑二千戶 「食」各本並作「侯」。

translations.literal: "A fief of two thousand households for bathing and maintenance": for shi all editions alike read hou.
translations.idiomatic: On "a fief of two thousand households for maintenance": all editions read hou for shi.

sentences.zh: 據御覽一五二改。

translations.literal: Changed on the authority of the Imperial Readings 152.
translations.idiomatic: Emended per Imperial Readings 152.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書 「讀書」各本並作「講書」，據南史、元龜一九二、御覽一二八引改。

translations.literal: "The emperor from youth loved reading": for "reading" all editions alike read "lecturing"; changed on the authority of the History of the Southern Dynasties, Yuan Gui 192, and the citation in Imperial Readings 128.
translations.idiomatic: On "from youth the emperor loved reading": all editions read lecturing for reading; emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties, Yuan Gui 192, and Imperial Readings 128.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁山陽王休祐領之 各本並脫「休仁山陽王」五字，據南史補。

translations.literal: "Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge of them": all editions alike omit the five characters "Xiuren Prince of Shanyang Wang."
translations.idiomatic: On "Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge": all editions omit the five characters naming both princes.

sentences.zh: 張燴讀史舉正云：「按建安王乃休仁，休祐則山陽王也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hui's Corrections in Reading History says: "According to this, Prince of Jian'an is Xiuren, and Xiuyou is Prince of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui's Corrections in Reading History states: "Prince of Jian'an is Xiuren, and Xiuyou is Prince of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 南史作『以建安王休仁、山陽王休祐領之』為是。」

translations.literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties' reading 'Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge of them' is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Southern Dynasties' version—'Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were put in charge of them'—is correct."
